explanation: Emberá hunters rubbed dart tips on the frog's back. Captive-bred frogs are harmless, because wild ones are thought to get their poison from the insects they eat.

claims.text: Emberá hunters in Colombia have tipped blowgun darts with toxin from the skin of the golden poison frog (Phyllobates terribilis).
Cane toads, coral snakes and Gila monsters were not the source of Colombian blowgun dart poison.
Hunters prepared darts by rubbing the tips on the frog's back.
Captive-bred golden poison frogs are not toxic.
Wild golden poison frogs are thought to obtain their toxins from insects in their diet.
